Indexes

1. Why Indexes Matter
  • Without indexes, SQL queries must scan every entry in the cache (full scan);
  • Indexes allow the query engine to quickly locate matching rows without scanning everything;
  • Properly designed indexes can improve query performance by orders of magnitude;
2. Creating Indexes
  • Via SQL: 
    -- Single-column index
CREATE INDEX idx_person_city ON Person (city);

-- Composite index
CREATE INDEX idx_person_city_age ON Person (city, age);

-- Descending index
CREATE INDEX idx_person_age_desc ON Person (age DESC);

-- Drop an index
DROP INDEX idx_person_city;
  • Via annotations (Java): 
    public class Person {
    @QuerySqlField(index = true)
    private String city;

    @QuerySqlField(index = true, descending = true)
    private int age;

    @QuerySqlField  // queryable but not indexed
    private String name;
}
  • Via QueryEntity configuration: 
    QueryEntity queryEntity = new QueryEntity(Integer.class, Person.class);

LinkedHashMap<String, String> fields = new LinkedHashMap<>();
fields.put("name", String.class.getName());
fields.put("city", String.class.getName());
fields.put("age", Integer.class.getName());
queryEntity.setFields(fields);

queryEntity.setIndexes(Arrays.asList(
    new QueryIndex("city"),
    new QueryIndex(Arrays.asList("city", "age"), QueryIndexType.SORTED)
));

CacheConfiguration cfg = new CacheConfiguration("PersonCache");
cfg.setQueryEntities(Collections.singletonList(queryEntity));
3. Index Types
TypeDescription
SORTED (default)B+ tree index; supports equality, range, and ordering queries
FULLTEXTLucene-based full-text search index for text fields
GEOSPATIALSpatial index for geographic queries (requires ignite-geospatial module)
4. Inline Index Size
  • Ignite can store part of the indexed value inline in the B+ tree pages;
  • This reduces I/O because the query engine can compare values without fetching the full data page;
  • Configure inline size: 
    CREATE INDEX idx_person_name ON Person (name) INLINE_SIZE 30;
  • Rule of thumb: set inline size to the typical length of the indexed field value + a few bytes overhead;
5. Best Practices
  • Index columns used in WHERE, JOIN, and ORDER BY clauses;
  • Use composite indexes for queries that filter on multiple columns — order the columns by selectivity (most selective first);
  • Avoid over-indexing: each index consumes memory and slows down writes;
  • Use EXPLAIN to verify that your query uses the expected index: 
    EXPLAIN SELECT * FROM Person WHERE city = 'NYC';
